topic: Resuscitation and physical health equipment on psychiatric wards
usual_baseline: Equipment is usually partly available: 66–90% of standards met. Missing or expired adrenaline, suction and masks in 7/10 locations [3356]; 70% of weekly checklists wrong. One learning disability unit had no trolley [3046]. Small items such as testing pins, Snellen charts and ophthalmoscopes are borrowed between wards [3647].
fix_that_works: Equipment boxes in clinic rooms: availability 66% to 73.5% [3069]. Weekly checks, maintenance registration and complete sets: resuscitation equipment 94.2% to 99.2% [3220]. An updated local protocol left trolleys better stocked [3046].
fix_that_fails: Physical health equipment fell from 83.8% to 76.6% despite the same interventions [3220]. Secure wards still lagged controls [3069]. Items added to trolleys were hard to find [3046].
consultant_advice: A quick audit, but resuscitation kit tends to improve once weekly checks are enforced. Physical health kit is the neglected side. Measure whether it is working and used, with a named checker, rather than just counting items.
